title: Initial Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) Method Registrations
summary: Registers the HTTP methods that were defined in RFCs before the IANA HTTP Method Registry was established, giving that registry its initial contents.

plainLanguage.summary: A new list of web request types was started. This document adds all the older, already existing types to the list.

questions: what is the http method registry
subtitle: Registers HTTP methods in the IANA method registry.

tldr.problem: HTTP methods existed before an IANA registry was established, with no single authoritative list.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7237 registers all previously-defined HTTP methods into the new IANA registry with their safe and idempotent properties.
tldr.outcome: Future extensions have a central registry to register new methods and check for conflicts.

today: RFC 7237 is an Internet Standard and is still the initial registration list for the IANA HTTP Method Registry.

sections.title: Registration of HTTP Methods
sections.content:
HTTP methods like GET, POST, PUT and DELETE are fundamental to web communication. Over time, extensions added new methods: PATCH for partial updates, PROPFIND to query document properties, LOCK to prevent concurrent edits, and many more for protocols like WebDAV, CalDAV and versioning systems.

RFC 7231 established the IANA HTTP Method Registry, but it was created after most of these methods existed. RFC 7237 registers all 34 previously-defined methods into this new registry with their defining RFCs and key properties: whether they are safe (read-only) and idempotent (repeatable without side effects).
sections.plainLanguage: The new official list of web request types needed to include all the old ones that already existed. This document adds them all at once.

sections.title: The Registered Methods
sections.content: The registered methods fall into several categories. Core HTTP methods come from early RFCs: GET and HEAD for retrieval, POST for submission, PUT for replacement, DELETE for removal. WebDAV methods handle document management: COPY, MOVE, DELETE (for resources), MKCOL (make collection), LOCK and UNLOCK for concurrency control, and PROPFIND/PROPPATCH for managing properties. Versioning extensions add CHECKIN, CHECKOUT, MERGE, UPDATE and related methods. CalDAV for calendaring adds MKCALENDAR. Some methods like PATCH are safe (idempotent) and can be repeated; others like LOCK require careful handling because repeating them has different effects.
sections.plainLanguage: Different tools added different request types: some to move or copy files, some to lock them so two people do not edit at once, some for calendars. Now they all have registered names.

sections.title: Safe and Idempotent Properties
sections.content: Each registered method has two important properties. A safe method does not modify the server: GET and HEAD are safe; POST is not. An idempotent method has the same result whether sent once or multiple times: PUT and DELETE are idempotent (the third DELETE of a resource is like the second or first), but LOCK is not (it fails if already locked). Knowing these properties helps servers and clients decide how to handle retries and caching.
sections.plainLanguage: Some requests ask questions (safe); others change things. Some are okay to send twice (idempotent); others are not. The list tells you which is which.

sections.title: The IANA Registry
sections.content: By registering these methods in the IANA HTTP Method Registry, future protocol designers have a single authoritative source to check for existing methods and to avoid collisions. When a new RFC proposes a novel HTTP method, it must be registered, which prompts review and documentation of its semantics. The registry prevents different protocols from accidentally using the same method name with different meanings.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry is the official place to check if a method name is taken before inventing a new one.
